citations.quote: Leaves can be toxic to pets, particularly dogs and cats.

citations.source: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
citations.quote: This plant contains calcium oxalate crystals, which are toxic if ingested or if the juice/sap is touched (dermatitis). More so a concern for dogs, cats, and horses but can also a concern for humans.

unknowns: No field in this record was refuted or removed by either audit.
The NC State profile used is the genus-level Aglaonema page and Clemson's factsheet is also genus-level. Clemson's HGIC 1450 light table is the only source that names A. commutatum specifically.
chill_damage_f conflict within Clemson: the quick-guide says avoid below 55 F, the body text says sensitive to chilling below 50 F. 55 is recorded because it is the more protective of the two.

humidity_need: Clemson says low to moderate household humidity, NC State says the plant prefers high humidity but tolerates drier air. 'average' is a split-the-difference between two non-overlapping statements, not an overlap, and neither source gives percentages.
night_f_min/max: Clemson gives a single 68-80 F band without splitting day and night.
humidity_pct_min/max: no named source states percentages.
light_dli_min/opt_low/opt_high: no authoritative source publishes DLI for this species.
water_growing_days_est and water_dormant_days_est: Clemson gives a dry-down depth cue but no interval; NC State says only to reduce watering in winter.
soil_base: neither source names a specific medium.
soil_ph_min: NC State records only the Acid (<6.0) category, which has no stated lower bound.
fertilize_active_months/interval_days/strength: neither source gives a feeding schedule.
outdoor_sun_exposure: houseplant record; indoor light values are not converted.
Clemson HGIC 1450's species table is excerpted from the SC Master Gardener Training Manual EC 678, originally published 09/99.
Clemson's Chinese Evergreen factsheet ends by pointing readers to the ASPCA toxic plant list. That list was not opened, cited, or reproduced.

removals.reason: Auditors disagreed (upheld at 6 by the sourcing audit, refuted as incoherent with a 200 ft-c good-light figure by the horticultural audit, which proposed 2). Conservative outcome applied: null.

Refuted by both audits: a 180-day cadence with no season anchor either never fires or schedules a midwinter feed on a dormant rhizome that cannot flush salts. No source names months, so the interval cannot be anchored.
Refuted. The suggested April-September is not stated by any cited source; Clemson says only 'growing season'.

Unsupported. Clemson's quoted recipe is an amended standard potting mix, not a cactus or succulent medium, and a true gritty mix would contradict the record's own 15-day summer watering cadence. Auditors split on the replacement value, so null.

Refuted. 200 ft-c is a whole-category preferred band from a 1999 interiorscape table, roughly DLI 1.7 - maintenance light, not good-growth light for a foliage aroid, and it contradicts NC State asking for more light for variegated cultivars.

Auditors disagreed. Clemson gives 50-70% as preferred and says pothos tolerates the 30-60% home range, so a 50% floor turns a preference into a requirement. Suggested revision to 30 was not accepted under the disagreement rule; null.
Refuted. A 55 F night ceiling against a 65 F day floor leaves 55-65 F satisfying neither, so no household temperature passes. Clemson states 50-55 F as ideal, not as a limit.
Unsupported. Neither cited page establishes the epithet: NC State's is the genus profile and Clemson writes the taxon as the hybrid Spathiphyllum x 'Wallisii'. The caveat now lives in name_note.
